proposal_contract.observed_problem_or_opportunity: Taking both MU and SKHX would concentrate the non-crypto expansion in semiconductors. MU has the better strategy lead, while WTI offers a different risk driver and sufficient liquidity for a prospective challenger.
proposal_contract.applicable_market_regime: MU applies only to its frozen 15m upward breakout-pressure conditions. The CL hypothesis is prospective and must not claim a regime edge until new long and short observations resolve.
proposal_contract.alternatives_considered: Use both semiconductor names, select SILVER, revive Gold or Brent, add CL bidirectionally, or leave the slot open. Both semiconductors concentrate risk; SILVER is forward-negative; Gold and Brent require new mechanisms; failed CL shorts cannot be silently retained.
proposal_contract.expected_upside: A single semiconductor plus a commodity mechanism could increase opportunity breadth without duplicating the same industry exposure.
proposal_contract.main_risks_and_failure_modes: Post-hoc long-side selection, unresolved historical CL mark paths, observer source-transport mismatch, sparse prospective episodes, oil-specific gap and roll behavior, funding and fee changes, and correlation instability.
proposal_contract.validation_completed: Current venue liquidity and candle continuity were observed; MU versus SKHX was compared at intended-size capacity; SILVER was re-evaluated on ten exact forward onsets; CL restarted from a fresh no-hindsight cursor with no signer or order surface.

proposal_contract.success_metrics: MU remains positive after friction and winner removal with both sides represented; CL produces positive prospective route-native economics without selecting away adverse shorts; both resolve all source and lifecycle evidence; combined portfolio stress remains acceptable.
proposal_contract.failure_or_rollback_triggers: Negative MU expanded-window robustness, no MU shorts, negative or winner-dependent CL prospective economics, source mismatch, roll/session anomalies, excessive intended-size slippage, or correlated losses inconsistent with the diversification hypothesis.
